analysis:
Reviewed scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (both base_text units, lines 1-966) and the changed ranges in the patch excerpt. The PR change is test-only: it adds a HOURLY = "ci-dev-hourly.yml" constant (head lines 134-136), adds that workflow to the classified-workflow set in test_every_workflow_is_classified (head ~709-710), and adds test_hourly_full_run_only_dispatches_ci_dev_on_dev (head ~954-972). The patch excerpt is truncated, so the assertions in the new test are not fully visible. The new workflow ci-dev-hourly.yml itself is not in the supplied evidence; the new test asserts: schedule and workflow_dispatch triggers only, cron '7 * * * *', top-level permissions {}, and a GitHub-hosted ubuntu runner. The remaining assertions are unseen.

No production code or security control changes. The test file adds no new attack surface. Existing guards are unchanged, including the no-secrets/no-id-token/read-only router checks, the unrouted-workflow literal-runner checks, and the rule that no non-router workflow may contain self-hosted/darkbloom labels (the new hourly workflow falls under that loop).

The threat model's provider, coordinator and cache threats (T-041 etc.) are not touched. Remaining integration question: the actual ci-dev-hourly.yml, which dispatches CI on dev with presumably actions:write permission, is outside the supplied units and was not reviewed. Its token scope, ref pinning and any use of secrets cannot be verified here. Because the new test's assertions beyond the visible lines are cut off, whether it enforces least privilege for the dispatch job is unverified. This is a CI-governance concern that is not part of the provider threat model, so it is not a finding.
